bib.title: Chain of Draft: Thinking Faster by Writing Less

question: Can an LLM reason with minimal per-step drafts instead of verbose chain of thought and keep accuracy while cutting tokens and latency?
hypothesis: Concise per-step drafts (at most five words) preserve CoT accuracy at a fraction of the tokens.
contributions: We introduce Chain of Draft, a concise reasoning prompting strategy inspired by human cognitive processes.
We empirically validate that Chain of Draft can achieve significantly reduced latency and cost without sacrificing accuracy.
We discuss the implications of Chain of Draft for LLM design, deployment, and real-world usability.

method.summary: Prompting only: a system prompt asks for step-by-step thinking with at most five words per step, plus few-shot examples with hand-written drafts. Compared against Standard and CoT prompts on GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet over GSM8K, BIG-bench date and sports understanding, and a synthetic coin flip set.

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.size: 8,500 grade-school problems as described; test size used not stated

datasets.name: Coin flip (synthesized)
datasets.source: Synthesized after Wei et al. 2022; 4 names randomly chosen from top 1000 US first names in NameDataset (Remy 2021), each randomly flips or not

inference.prompting: Few-shot for Standard, CoT (exact examples from CoT paper appendix, answer after ####) and CoD (authors hand-wrote a draft for each few-shot example); number of shots not stated. Zero-shot variant in Table 5.

parameters.words_per_step: 5 at most, a guideline not enforced

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of correct final answers, extracted after ####

metrics.name: Latency
metrics.definition: average response latency; measurement setup not described

eval.protocol: Single run per cell as reported; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests stated.

prompts.text: Answer the question directly. Do not return any preamble, explanation, or reasoning.
Think step by step to answer the following question. Return the answer at the end of the response after a separator ####.
Think step by step, but only keep a minimum draft for each thinking step, with 5 words at most. Return the answer at the end of the response after a separator ####.

limits: Zero-shot CoD is much weaker: Claude gains only 3.6% over direct answering and token savings shrink (Table 5).
Small models (under 3B) show larger CoD to CoT gaps; fine-tuning on CoD data is proposed but untested.
Authors hypothesise CoD-style patterns are scarce in training data; not tested.
Five-word limit is not enforced; no check of actual adherence.
Only two proprietary models in the main results; decoding settings, shot count, test sizes and latency method not stated; no seeds or significance.
Coin flip data is self-synthesized, not the original; ceiling at 100% for CoT and CoD.
No reasoning-model (o1, R1) comparison despite motivation.
